v2_1_before_blind.safety_pass_before_freeze: After these numbers were first reached, v2.0 and v2.1 were run side by side on about ninety hand-written texts outside the perturbation pool (postponements, cancellations, recitals, modified terms, paid amounts). The development build committed some of them wrongly while scoring 0 wrong on all five corpora. Removed: a shortcut that ignored an unknown date falling after the driving deadline. Added, all abstaining: sole_candidate on N-008, vetoes N-V01 / N-V02, across_a_date on N-002 / N-007 / N-008, limits on N-009, mood rules TC-M03..TC-M05, after_not on A-002 / A-003. The aggregates of the five corpora are identical before and after the pass: the corpora cannot see what it fixed. Tried and dropped: a PEC subject naming another act as a veto on the title (cost 2 / 4 / 3 correct document types on the perturbed corpora; the corpus plants misleading subjects and its gold follows the title).
v2_1_before_blind.how_much_is_general: Not measurable on these corpora. The perturbed suites contain only the eleven rewrites of corpus/perturb.py; eight of them touch deadline, type or amount reading and every one of them is inside what v2.1 reads. A table of those eight phrasings would have produced the same numbers. What the structural mechanisms add is tested only by unit tests on wordings outside the pool (tests/test_termclauses.py, tests/test_v21_mechanisms.py), written by the same author as the rules.
v2_1_before_blind.remaining_gap: record-level RECUPERARE rate stays above expected because of sender_class abstentions (lawyer on a generic domain without 'Avv.': abstention by design, unchanged in v2.1).
